**Reading map:** Deisenroth, Faisal & Ong, *Mathematics for Machine Learning* (2020), §3.7. This is an original lesson using our delivery-operations example—not reproduced textbook content.

## Why the concept matters

Vectors are not always finite lists of numbers. We can also compare signals or functions using an integral, which extends geometric intuition to function spaces.

## Define the mathematical relationship

$$
\langle f,g\rangle=\int_a^b f(t)g(t)\,dt
$$

The displayed relationship is the main object to analyse. Specify the relevant dimensions, quantities and assumptions before using it. It should be read as a mathematical statement, not merely a programming shorthand.

## Work through an original example

On [0,1], let f(t)=1 and g(t)=t. Their inner product is integral_0^1 t dt=1/2. The squared norm of g is integral_0^1 t^2 dt=1/3, hence ||g||=sqrt(1/3).

## What follows, and what does not

The precise function space and integrability assumptions matter. This continuous analogy prepares the reader for functional approximation and kernel methods.

## Test your reasoning

What is the inner product of 1 and t-1/2 on [0,1]?
